findings.title: The new document-page section tells a person their SUCCESSFULLY posted payslip 'was not posted again -- open that entry to decide whether this is a correction or a re-upload'
findings.evidence: Ticket line: 'The document page's payroll panel then says why a summary did not post, reading the new door rather than the queue.' PayrollPostingSection (apps/web/components/documents/payroll-posting-section.tsx:88-99) renders state.sentence verbatim for EVERY payroll_summary with no gate on verdict or rung, and is mounted unconditionally for that kind on the accounting tab (apps/web/components/documents/document-detail.tsx:396-402). But clara._payroll_posting_verdict reaches rung 10 no_duplicate_entry with scope same_document for a payslip whose OWN entry stands on it (packages/db/migrations/0343_payroll_completeness_witness.sql:1665-1672, v_dup_entry := clara._document_posting_entry(v_client, p_document)), and 0343:1846-1852 builds the sentence 'Payroll run %s is already posted (%s, %s). This payslip was not posted again -- open that entry to decide whether this is a correction or a re-upload.' DRIVEN ON clara_c01 through the estate's own doors (seedPayrollChart + readPayrollDoc for month 2026-11 on world.clients.A1, then select clara.get_payroll_posting_state($1) as alice): posted=true, entry a0544b62-3d9f-4986-ace0-9f029c122ef8, and the door answered {verdict:'blocked', rung:'no_duplicate_entry', reason:'duplicate_entry', sentence:'Payroll run November 2026 is already posted (Payroll run November 2026, 2026-11-30). This payslip was not posted again -- open that entry to decide whether this is a correction or a re-upload.'}. So on the happy path the accounting tab reads 'A posted entry of <client> currently stands on this document.' immediately followed by 'Payroll posting' and that sentence. Neither battery reaches the state: the six db cells drive facts_read, completeness_witness, a foreign document, an unknown id, a non-payslip and the floor; the five component cells drive a blocked sentence, a parked question, a non-payroll page, a moved kind and a banner refusal.
findings.required_fix: Decide and test what the panel says when the verdict is not a genuine block for this document: either render nothing when rung is no_duplicate_entry and the duplicate's scope is same_document (the payslip's own entry), or give that case a settled sentence of the panel's own. Add a cell for a successfully posted payslip on both sides (db: drive the door against a posted run; web: the component for a posted state). If the behaviour is intended, it needs an explicit ruling rather than a silent render.

findings.title: plans_still_posting counts only plans citing the CURRENT instruction row, so after a second recording the card says 'Nothing was running under it, so nothing keeps posting' while a plan keeps posting
findings.evidence: Ticket line: 'The withdraw door's answer additionally carries the number of live plans that were authorised by the instruction being withdrawn, and the settings card states plainly, in a message key, that those plans keep posting under the member who authorised them.' The count keys on the ROW id (packages/db/migrations/0362_standing_instruction_agent_read.sql, B: and ap.authority_ref ->> 'id' = v_row.id::text). But 0338's record door is version-forward: a restated reason, or simply recording the instruction again after a withdrawal, supersedes the live row and inserts a fresh one with a new id (packages/db/migrations/0338_prepayment_close_standing_instruction.sql:436-468), while an already-authorised plan keeps citing the OLD id (0338:1102, jsonb_build_object('kind','firm_standing_instruction','id', v_si_id, ...)). DRIVEN ON clara_c01 through the human doors only (record -> real wake12 plan -> withdraw -> record -> withdraw): withdrawal 1 answered plans_still_posting=1, withdrawal 2 answered plans_still_posting=0, and the plan was STILL status='active' afterwards. A second probe took the restate path (record, plan, record with a new reason, withdraw) and also answered 0 with the plan active. The web module passes 0 straight through (apps/web/lib/firm/standing-instructions.ts:133-140) and the card renders standingWithdrawnPlans at count 0, whose text is 'Nothing was running under it, so nothing keeps posting.' (apps/web/messages/en.json) -- a positive false statement in exactly the situation the ticket exists to correct ('A firm that takes an instruction back reasonably believes it stopped something'). Both new count cells (p1147.withdraw.counts, p1147.withdraw.counts_only_what_still_posts) use a single instruction row per firm, so neither reaches this state.
findings.required_fix: Count the firm's live plans for the instruction KEY family rather than the single row id -- authority_ref ->> 'instruction_key' = v_key (0338 already writes that key into authority_ref) plus firm_id and status='active' -- or restrict the card's zero sentence to 'nothing keeps posting under this recording'. Add a cell for record -> plan -> withdraw -> record -> withdraw.

findings.title: The read door has no viewer-floor check; the ticket says 'at the viewer floor'
findings.evidence: Ticket line: 'A granted, security-definer, read-only door answers the firm's live standing instruction for the agent read role, firm-scoped through the caller's own context rather than a firm argument, at the viewer floor.' clara.wake_get_firm_standing_instruction (0362 A) performs no rank check at all: it resolves clara.wake_context(), asks the allowlist and requires an on_behalf_of. The migration states the reasoning (A, bullet 3) and the lane drives it: p1147.read.floor_is_the_credential shows a viewer reading the relation herself AND clara.mint_wake_credential refusing CLR10 to mint on a viewer's behalf, so the reachable floor is bookkeeper+ -- strictly narrower than the ticket asked, never looser. Recorded so the merger does not read 'viewer floor' in the ticket and 'no floor' in the body as a gap.
findings.required_fix: None required. If a viewer-rank statement is wanted in the body for the day the credential floor moves, it is a successor edit, not this ticket's.

findings.title: A third refusal, CLR10 / not_a_payroll_summary, beyond the brief's refusal mapping
findings.evidence: The brief's Refusal mapping names only 'CLR11 not-found for a document that is not this firm's, CLR04 for the role floor, anything else surfacing verbatim as a door refusal.' 0363 A adds a kind gate raising CLR10 with detail {"reason":"not_a_payroll_summary"}, and the web module and section carry a dedicated arm for it (isNotAPayrollSummary, rendered as silence). The reasoning is sound and written out (0363 A(2b); reports/waveK-lane01-ticket1148.md section 3): without it the door handed an invoice would answer 'This payroll summary has not been read yet.' over a supplier bill. p1148.read.kind proves the firm wall is asked FIRST, so the kind refusal is no cross-firm oracle. Flagged only because it is an addition to the contract the brief wrote, and it is an arm the successor chat tool must carry.
findings.required_fix: None. Keep the refusal in the successor contract (section 8 of the ticket report already does) so the chat tool never surfaces it as a firm-facing sentence.

findings.title: The answer carries a sixth key, document_id, beyond the brief's five
findings.evidence: Ticket line: 'It projects the verdict's sentence, verdict, rung, reason and completeness, and not the whole rung_vector.' 0363 A returns those five plus document_id, which is the caller's own argument echoed back and carries no information the caller did not supply. p1148.read.projection pins the key set at exactly those six and asserts 'rung_vector' in r === false after first reading the internal as root to show the door NARROWS. No leak, no missing key.

findings.title: #1050's 'no machine twin by NAME' census becomes a property test that a future firm-argument read would pass
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/prepayment-close-standing-instruction.test.mjs (p1050.doors.shape) asserted kin.rows deepEqual [] for every clara function matching wake_%firm_standing_instruction% and its siblings. The diff replaces that with a filter admitting any such function that is STABLE and granted to clara_agent_ro and to no writer role. That is necessary -- 0362 mints exactly such a read and the file is frontier-gated at 0338, so a name roster would red every pre-0362 chain -- and the reasoning is written into the cell. The residue: a later wake_get_firm_standing_instruction_for(firm uuid) that is STABLE and agent_ro-granted would now pass this census, so the 'no firm argument' property that makes 0362's door a non-oracle is held only by p1147.read.no_oracle, not by the family census. Re-run: 18 pass / 0 fail.
findings.required_fix: Optional: have the census also refuse a matching body whose argument list names a firm, so the non-oracle property is held structurally as well as behaviourally.

summary: Both tickets are built, and every criterion but the from-scratch chain carries lane evidence that re-runs green (14 db cells, 26 web cells, CI lint exit 0). Two spec defects survive verification, both user-facing and both in states no cell reaches: #1148's new panel renders the verdict's re-file sentence on a payslip that posted perfectly well, telling the reader to decide whether it is a correction or a re-upload; and #1147's plans_still_posting keys on the instruction ROW rather than the key family, so a firm that records the instruction a second time is told at withdrawal that nothing keeps posting while a plan is still active. Both were driven on clara_c01 through the estate's own doors rather than argued from the code. The remainder are one orchestrator debt (the owner ruling the ticket asked to be recorded on #1147 is not on it), one integrator debt (the from-scratch chain, which the closing plan assigns away from the lane), and four notes.
